Write-ups and notes. We start by **describing** who gets drafted, then explore
associations, then build and honestly evaluate forecasts.

## What we know {#what-we-know}

Figures that started as an Investigations card and became a standing answer.
Each links back to the card it came from, where its code and terms are.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| output: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
root <- Sys.getenv("CFB2NFL_ROOT")
if (!nzchar(root)) root <- pkgload::pkg_path()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
pkgload::load_all(root, quiet = TRUE)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(
  duckdb::duckdb(),
  file.path(root, "data", "cfb2nfl.duckdb"),
  read_only = TRUE
)
risk <- eligible_risk_set(dplyr::collect(dplyr::tbl(con, "outcomes")))
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

### How often eligible seasons end in the NFL {#how-often-eligible-seasons-end-in-the-nfl}

Out of every hundred draft-eligible college seasons, about
`r round(100 * mean(risk$outcome_drafted_d))` end in a draft pick and about
`r round(100 * mean(risk$outcome_nfl_entry_d))` in the NFL by either route.
From the card [How often does an eligible college season end in the draft or
the NFL?](card-outcome-ledger.html).

```{r}
#| label: outcome-ledger
p <- plot_outcome_ledger(outcome_ledger(risk)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Share of eligible seasons ending in each NFL outcome",
    subtitle = "Eligible player-seasons with a known outcome",
    x = "Share of eligible seasons",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
card_interactive(p, height_svg = 5)
```

## Building the foundation first

Before fitting a single model, we built the scaffolding that makes results
trustworthy: a `targets` pipeline (the Pipeline page), data contracts that run
inside it, and a per-step audit log (the Data page) so any number we report can
be traced back to the rows and code that produced it.

The payoff was immediate. The audit log surfaced where the **long** stats
collapse to a player-season backbone, and where joining head coaches inflates
rows because some schools had more than one head coach in a season. Ingesting
`/roster` also taught us two things worth writing down: its `year` field is the
player's eligibility class, not the season (fixed by stamping the queried year,
lifting key coverage from ~29% to ~99.5%), and its weight is *static* per player
— so a between-season weight-change feature isn't derivable from it.

Those are exactly the silent data issues we never want to discover *after*
modeling. Next up: describe who gets drafted by position, team, and hometown.
